observed_mechanisms: Adjacent-frame mean absolute pixel distance is the primitive used for hue/saturation/luma/edge change components.
ContentDetector combines component deltas into a weighted frame score and supports luma-only operation.
AdaptiveDetector keeps a bounded 1+2*window_width score buffer and detects deviations from the local rolling mean, mitigating some fast-camera-motion false positives.
ContentDetector edge-kernel sizing is explicitly heuristic/TODO in upstream source and should not be imported as an F2 invariant.
Core project dependency declares numpy; the detector implementation imports cv2/OpenCV at runtime.
structural_similarity computes mean full-reference structural similarity with explicit windowing/channel/data-range semantics.
Floating-point inputs require explicit data_range; channel ranges such as YCbCr cannot be naively averaged under one common range.
The current wrapper delegates to the new skimage2 implementation rather than being a tiny standalone primitive.
The package dependency surface includes numpy, scipy, networkx, pillow, imageio, tifffile, packaging and lazy-loader.

source_pins.observed_scope: SSIM is a full-reference structural/perceptual image-quality similarity method; that scope is not identical to online temporal novelty/change detection.

f2_source_observations: CaptureBroker v3 stores immutable frame references only and explicitly does not persist raw frame bytes.
CaptureBroker maintains bounded live refs, bounded recent-drop diagnostics, monotonic source ordering and bounded rolling provenance.

Therefore any pixel-domain delta/quality measurement must be computed while transient frame pixels are available upstream of or adjacent to reference publication, then persisted only as typed derived measurement/provenance if admitted.

e1_findings.finding: F2 should keep temporal visual novelty/change and full-reference visual quality/similarity as separate typed measurements. A single SSIM-like score should not silently stand for both.

PySceneDetect source supports a much thinner baseline than importing its pipeline: adjacent-frame mean absolute luma difference is a deterministic, bounded-state candidate primitive; a small rolling baseline/ratio is a separate adaptive extension.

SSIM is technically useful as a secondary full-reference stability/quality discriminator when the comparison question requires structural similarity, but requires fixed data-range/window/channel semantics and should not be the default scene-change gate.

Importing the complete scikit-image stack solely for an SSIM hot-path primitive is not justified at E1 because its package surface is substantially broader than the F2 need. Thin structural distillation or an already-present lower-level image primitive should be tested first.

Importing the complete PySceneDetect detector pipeline is also not justified at E1. Its adjacent-frame delta and bounded adaptive-ratio ideas are separable from scene-cut orchestration, thresholds, flash filtering and heuristic edge handling.

hypothesis: A native typed RetinaDelta measurement containing a cheap luma-MAE novelty score plus optional bounded adaptive baseline will provide most of the online change-sensing value at lower dependency/state cost; SSIM should remain an optional separately typed reference-quality measurement.
counterhypotheses: Luma-only MAE may overreact to global illumination/exposure change and under-detect chromatic-only changes.
A small adaptive baseline may suppress genuinely important sustained changes or introduce detection latency.
Full SSIM or another structural metric may outperform luma MAE for some low-motion but semantically important changes.
If OpenCV/scikit-image is already an unavoidable F2 runtime dependency elsewhere, import-cost arguments weaken, though semantic separation and provenance requirements remain.
e2_required_mapping_questions: Where exactly in the Perception Fabric should transient pixels be consumed so raw-frame persistence remains false?
What typed schema binds source_id, previous/current frame_ref_id, sequences, metric version, parameters and derived scores without minting world truth?
Can a fixed downsample/grid and integer luma-MAE be made deterministic across supported hosts/backends?
What illumination, chromatic-only, camera-motion and no-change falsifier fixtures are required before any threshold is accepted?
Is OpenCV already an admitted dependency at the exact target runtime, or should the primitive avoid it entirely?
